task/tests/test.sh (lines 40-125 launch contract and health probe; 155-195 restart helper)
qc/runs/kittle-2026-10-09-r4/raw-evidence-index.json (hashes of server.js, app.js, solve.sh, seed and run_golden.sh re-verified as matching current bytes)
evidence: Runtime-fact half PASSES. Every hard fact the verifier relies on is stated publicly: entry /app/server.js (instruction.md:5; integration.md:3); start command Node 22 running server.js as an ordinary user, not necessarily from /app, files resolved relative to server.js (integration.md:3), matching test.sh:97-111 (setpriv uid 65534, env -i, possible $APP_COPY relocation); listen 0.0.0.0:3000 (integration.md:3; test.sh:108 PORT=3000); NODE_PATH globals (integration.md:3; environment/Dockerfile); storage /app/app.db or DB_PATH (instruction.md:5; integration.md:3; test.sh:98-109); GET /api/health 200 even without the DB (integration.md:3; test.sh:48 probes /api/health then /); fixed clock 2026-05-12T11:00:00Z (integration.md:7; seed 'clock'); seed /assets/seed_data.json copied to /app and imported once into an empty DB (instruction.md:5; integration.md:5); no leftover DB and no symlinks (integration.md:5; test.sh:71-82); accounts and password123 (walls-and-retention.md:3-11, matching seed and app_context.md:8-16); Dev walled from M-12 (walls-and-retention.md:15). Network is public, so no offline constraint is needed. Deliverables half: I traced each of the 16 functional, 2 gate, 5 polish and 4 visual criteria to public text. Walls on every route incl. plain not-available, mentions, pasted links and live wall add (walls-and-retention.md:15-19); client scope and signed-out denial (instruction.md:7; integration.md:9; walls-and-retention.md:17); timers incl. exact boundary, shortening deletes at once, off never restores, partner-only (walls-and-retention.md:23-25); hold scope, nobody deletes held, release applies the timer at once, typed 'On hold' (walls-and-retention.md:29; conversations.md:13); replies 3 levels deep in send order with quote (conversations.md:5); edits, earlier versions, stale-edit refusal keeping typed text, deleted-parent placeholder (conversations.md:9; walls-and-retention.md:25); formatting and literal markup everywhere (conversations.md:13); message links with preview / not available (conversations.md:17); mentions (conversations.md:21); per-person unread, same in every tab, new-messages line, mark unread, deleted not counted (conversations.md:25); idempotent resend and stable order in thread/search/transcript (conversations.md:29); live updates preserving draft/scroll/open thread (conversations.md:31); 390 px (conversations.md:33); search case-insensitive, current text only, click opens at message (walls-and-retention.md:33); transcript heading with number/title/generated time, author, sent time, edited, hold mark, versions of held edited messages, no chat controls (walls-and-retention.md:35); refusal reason stays next to the action (walls-and-retention.md:37); restart durability (integration.md:5). Seed facts quoted by criteria (M-11 7-day, M-13 30-day, K-10 exactly seven days old, K-11 one second younger, Insurer letter held 3 May, probate 2,400 version, Fenwick / heads of terms in M-12) all match seed_data.json. ONE GRADED DEMAND IS NOT ASKED FOR: functional criterion sent_once_in_order Part B (tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:216-217) requires 'Each shows the firm's fixed sent time: 11:00 in the thread (a date there is optional)' and fails the criterion 'if any of them shows a different sent time'. No public file asks the chat thread to display each message's sent time. The only time statements are integration.md:7 ('New messages, edits and transcripts carry that time') and walls-and-retention.md:35 (the transcript lists messages 'each with its author, sent time'); conversations.md:29 asks only for consistent ORDER in the thread, search and transcript. A clock time on each thread message is the golden's choice (solution/app/public/app.js:310 renders <time> via fmtTime), not a stated requirement; qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md 'No hidden requirements': 'A default chosen by the golden is not automatically a requirement' and 'every graded demand needs a public requirement'. Minor Note (not a defect): 'following the link opens the matter at that message' (wall_mentions_and_links, message_links) is only implicit in conversations.md:17 and walls-and-retention.md:17 ('following an old link'), but it is the ordinary meaning of a message link. No configured judge run bears on this row; the raw-evidence index holds only scripted golden observations, which cannot show how a conforming alternative would score.
counterexample: Conforming alternative that fails: an app that implements every public rule, keeps C, A, B order everywhere, de-duplicates the replayed JUDGE-D1 request and shows '2026-05-12 11:00' for each message in the transcript, but shows no per-message time in the chat thread (or a relative label such as 'just now' / '8 days ago' against the fixed clock). The judge cannot see '11:00 in the thread', so sent_once_in_order (weight 2.5 of 33 functional) scores 0, also discarding the explicitly required idempotent-resend and ordering behaviour bundled into the same binary criterion. The thread-time leg adds no needed discrimination: a wrong clock is already caught by the transcript sent-time check in the same Part B.
suggested_fix: Either add a public sentence (e.g. in conversations.md 'Sending and live updates': 'each message in the thread shows who sent it and when') or drop '11:00 in the thread (a date there is optional)' from sent_once_in_order Part B and keep the sent-time check on the transcript, which walls-and-retention.md:35 already requires; then recheck app_context.md:28 and the criterion together as one candidate.
